correctness.rationale: For a common strict ranking, SD-EF1 for every ordered agent pair is equivalent to all preference-prefix bundle counts differing by at most one: removing the earliest item of an envied bundle suffices and any >=2 prefix gap obstructs. At prefix ell every agent must receive one of top ell goods; t=N-ell<ell remaining goods go to distinct agents. In a complete multipartite graph a bottom good can only join the top good from its own part, yielding the exact falling factorial and feasibility 2x_i<=n_i. Uniform bottom t-set yields the coefficient/hypergeometric probability. Worst-case threshold N-floor(min n_i/2) follows by putting excess low-ranked goods in a smallest part and monotonicity for lower agent counts. For K_{m,m}, the centered hypergeometric window has variance (m^2-s^2)/(4(2m-1)), giving 2Phi(sqrt2 c)-1=erf(c) for s/sqrt m->c; Chebyshev handles s/sqrt m->infty. Independently enumerated feasible shared-ranking allocations in (2,2) ell=3 (6), (2,3) ell=3 (0), (1,2,2) ell=3 (0).

value.rationale: PASS: Exact share of rankings admitting full SD-EF1 allocation is a natural reliability statistic that answers a different question from a worst-case strong-colorability threshold. The sharp erf(c) crossover demonstrates a genuine sqrt(m) typical-versus-linear worst-case gap, and the labelled-allocation coefficient polynomial quantifies the feasible solution multiplicity. No new broad mechanism theorem is required.

final_claim: For complete multipartite item-conflict graph, shared strict ranking, and N/2<ell<=N labelled agents, SD-EF1 feasibility iff each graph part has at most half its goods in bottom t=N-ell positions, with exact allocation count ell! product_i(n_i-x_i)_{x_i}; balanced bicliques have an erf square-root agent-surplus reliability transition, plus sharp all-ranking threshold.
limitations: Only N/2<ell<=N for count/probability, common strict order; weak orders only at worst-case threshold.
